title: Corporate Ownership and Evictions in Boston
description: An exploratory data analysis of how corporate landlords are distributed across Boston and how their presence relates to eviction patterns from 2004–2024.
story: For this assignment I wanted to go beyond a single choropleth and instead build a small analytic tool for myself. I started by cleaning the City of Boston ownership and eviction records, then experimented with views that let me compare corporate and individual landlords across neighborhoods. The final piece helped me see how a handful of companies drive a large share of filings, and it sparked questions about how policy could better target those owners.

title: Life Expectancy vs. GDP Interactive Scatterplot
description: A D3-based scatterplot that visualizes the relationship between GDP per capita and life expectancy for countries around the world.
story: This project was my first serious attempt at building an interactive chart from scratch. I spent a lot of time tuning the scales and tooltips so that hovering felt smooth and informative, not overwhelming. Seeing clusters of countries emerge—especially outliers that were rich but unhealthy, or poor but surprisingly long-lived—made me appreciate how much nuance a simple scatterplot can hold.

title: Transit Equity in Greater Boston
description: A map-based visualization comparing transit access across Boston neighborhoods with demographic and income data.
story: I built this project to understand how evenly public transit serves different communities in and around Boston. The workflow combined GTFS feeds with census data, which forced me to think carefully about spatial joins and unreliable shapes. The result is a set of small multiples that make it painfully obvious which neighborhoods wait the longest for service while also facing higher costs and lower incomes.

title: MIT Course Explorer Dashboard
description: A dashboard that lets students filter, search, and compare MIT courses using enrollment, evaluation, and scheduling information.
story: Choosing classes at MIT can feel like solving a puzzle, so I tried to turn that puzzle into a visual interface. I stitched together open datasets on enrollment and evaluation scores and designed a layout that surfaces trade-offs between workload, satisfaction, and time of day. The most satisfying part was watching friends use the tool and discover courses they would never have found in the vanilla catalog.

title: AI Policy Timeline
description: A narrative timeline that tracks major AI policy milestones, from early research funding decisions to recent regulatory proposals.
story: Because my research lives at the intersection of AI and policy, I wanted a way to visually trace how the conversation has evolved. I curated key moments from hearings, strategy documents, and public letters, then arranged them on an interactive timeline that highlights themes like safety, competition, and rights. The piece doubles as a personal reference I use when writing or teaching about the field.

title: Climate Pledges vs. Emissions
description: Linked views that contrast countries’ climate pledges with their historical and projected emissions.
story: This project began with a simple question: how closely do national climate pledges line up with the trajectories implied by their emissions data? I paired a ranking view with detailed country profiles so that clicking on a bar reveals a richer emissions history. Building the interaction pushed me to think about how to keep context visible while still inviting deep dives into individual cases.

title: Personal Reading Tracker
description: A small web app that visualizes my reading habits by genre, format, and time of year.
story: I built this project partly to justify my book-buying habit and partly to practice designing with real personal data. The interface uses simple shapes and colors, but it tells me at a glance when I am neglecting fiction or reading too many policy reports in a row. It has become a quiet dashboard for balance in my life outside of coursework.

title: Portfolio Landing Page Redesign
description: A responsive redesign of my personal portfolio homepage focused on clarity, accessibility, and storytelling.
story: This project was less about data and more about how to frame it. I iterated through several layouts and color systems, trying to create a landing page that feels welcoming but still professional. Along the way I paid particular attention to typography and contrast so that the site works well for visitors on different devices and with different accessibility needs.

title: Future Studio Project (Placeholder)
description: A placeholder slot reserved for an upcoming studio or research project.
story: This card marks space for a project I am still designing—most likely something that connects AI safety concepts to an interactive explanation aimed at a general audience. Keeping a visible placeholder here reminds me that my portfolio is a living document, not a static archive. By the end of the semester, this slot will hold a fully realized piece instead of just a promise.
